meta.genre: psychological thriller with slow-burn female intimacy, domestic noir, and a four-tier twist structure. First-person unreliable narrator.

title: The Quiet Wife
sub_niche: psychological thriller with slow-burn female intimacy, domestic noir, and a four-tier twist structure. First-person unreliable narrator.
hook_central: A live-in housekeeper believes she's rescuing a fragile wife from a controlling husband — until she discovers the wife hired her to be framed for murder, and both women have been lying since day one.

female.name: the housekeeper (unnamed narrator)
female.voice: I watch people. That's how I survive. I notice the way a man holds his glass, the tremor in a woman's hand, the seconds of silence that mean more than words.
tics: Touches her left earlobe when lying
female.boundary: Nora will not kill directly — she will manipulate others into doing it for her. She draws the line at physical violence against the innocent, but she will let a guilty person die if it serves her purpose.
female.internal_voice: I came here to bleed this family dry. But the wife — she's different. She sees me. And that terrifies me.

male.name: Unassigned (no male lead)
male.voice: My wife is unwell. You must be patient with her. She has episodes. I trust you to keep her safe — that's why I hired you.
tics: Never raises his voice, even when angry
male.boundary: Julian will never physically harm his wife, but he will control her through isolation and gaslighting. He believes he is protecting her from the world, not imprisoning her.
male.wound: His first wife died under mysterious circumstances — he was never charged, but the suspicion haunts him.

supporting_cast.name: Elena Ashford
supporting_cast.secret: She is the true architect of the frame — she hired Nora specifically because of her criminal past.

supporting_cast.name: Elena Ashford
supporting_cast.secret: She is not as fragile as she appears; she has been planning her husband's murder for years.

supporting_cast.name: Dr. Margaret Lin
supporting_cast.secret: She is aware of Elena's mental state but has been manipulated into prescribing sedatives that Elena hides instead of takes.

supporting_cast.name: Cora Baines
supporting_cast.secret: Cora was the previous housekeeper who 'left suddenly' — she was killed by Elena after discovering the plan.

central_mystery.question: Who is conning whom, and who dies?
central_mystery.answer: The wife engineered the entire hire to frame the housekeeper for the husband's murder, choosing her precisely because her criminal past makes her disposable and believable as a killer. The husband is not the predator; he is the target. The housekeeper is also running a con (she came to rob or blackmail this family), but the wife's con is deeper and older. The deepest betrayal: the one ally the housekeeper (and the reader) trusted most is the trap.

bloodline.description: No blood relations among leads. Nora is an only child of deceased parents (both died in a car accident when she was 12). Julian has no siblings; his parents are alive but estranged. Elena has a younger brother living abroad. No shared ancestry.
hard_rules: female_lead and male_lead are not blood relatives
female_lead and female supporting lead (Elena) are not blood relatives
male_lead and female supporting lead (Elena) are married, not blood related

world_rules: The story takes place in a wealthy suburban estate in upstate New York, isolated by woods.
Time is present-day, no supernatural elements.
All twists must be supported by physical evidence (documents, objects, recordings) found by the narrator.
The reader's understanding must be overturned every 2-3 chapters via a seed or shift.
No character confesses the truth in a monologue; truth is always discovered.

series_arc.thesis: Nora arrives at the Ashford estate believing she is conning a wealthy family; she forms a bond with Elena, whom she sees as a victim. By the end, she discovers Elena orchestrated everything to frame her for Julian's murder. Nora survives but is now complicit in the cover-up.
series_arc.ending_hook: Nora holds the planted evidence that could prove her innocence — but using it would expose her own criminal past. She burns it. The final line: 'I am now exactly who she needed me to be.'

content_rules: No explicit violence against animals or children.
Consent and psychological safety of vulnerable characters must be respected in narrative treatment.
